title: Mapping drivers of life expectancy change in Asia from 1990 to 2023.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, no open full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. Fetched the GBD (Global Burden of Disease) Results Tool landing page (HTTP 200, a JavaScript app); no direct file download was reachable without the interactive tool.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: 34 Asian countries/territories, 1990-2023, life expectancy, cause-specific mortality and risk factors, all taken from GBD 2023 estimates. That the GBD Results Tool requires a free IHME (Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation) account to download is from prior knowledge, not confirmed in this session.

a1_downloadable.note: No data of the paper's own; the inputs are GBD 2023 estimates served via the IHME Results Tool, which (per prior knowledge, not verified here) needs an account login to export. Not checked in files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Life expectancy and cause-specific death rates would be columns in a GBD export; not verified in files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Risk-factor exposures and covariates are available as GBD columns per country-year; not verified in files.

a4_units_stated.note: GBD exports state metric (rate, number, percent) and units; from prior knowledge, not checked.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unit of analysis is the country-year: 34 countries x 34 years is about 1,156 highly autocorrelated rows, below the ~1,500 threshold; effective independent n is ~34 countries.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without the export; no conflict seen.

a8_label_provenance.note: Every GBD number (life expectancy, cause-specific mortality, risk-attributable burden) is itself a model output (CODEm cause-of-death ensemble models, DisMod-MR, spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression) that already uses the same covariates as inputs; predicting it from GBD covariates would distil IHME's models, not learn from measurements.

backbone.name: none (country-year tabular data; no matching pretrained backbone)

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether socioeconomic indicators explain regional life-expectancy gains, but the GBD side is model-derived so the join would mostly recover GBD's own covariates.

controls.positive_control: Recover the COVID-19 drop in life expectancy in 2020-2021 reported in the abstract.
controls.external_validation: UN World Population Prospects life tables (also modelled, partly independent).

honest_claim_h3: A model would only predict IHME's modelled life expectancy estimates from IHME's own covariates for 34 Asian countries, not measured mortality.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use country-level risk-factor and development indicators to predict yearly life expectancy across 34 Asian countries.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per country per year (34 countries x 1990-2023, roughly 1,156 rows, not verified), with modelled risk-factor exposures as features.
plain_idea.predict: Life expectancy at birth per country-year, which comes from the Global Burden of Disease Study's own statistical models rather than a direct measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Health-policy analysts would see which risks track gains, but the answer largely restates the source models' assumptions.

ml_idea: Predict country-year life expectancy or cause-specific mortality from GBD risk-factor exposures; rejected because labels are GBD model outputs built from the same covariates.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only; nothing downloaded or timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Confirm whether the GBD Results Tool export works without an IHME login; label provenance (A8) kills it regardless.

verdict_reason: Fails A8: all labels are Global Burden of Disease model estimates derived from the same covariates, so any model would distil IHME's pipeline. Also fails A5 (about 1,156 autocorrelated country-years from 34 countries) and likely A1 (the export needs an IHME account login, not verified here). The paper itself releases no new data.
